deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics and is not a Riemann manuscript. It is the first page of a personal letter in German Kurrent script, signed off on the following pages. From the handwriting, the place names (Harzburg; return of the papers to Braunschweig in October) and the content, it is almost certainly from Richard Dedekind to Heinrich Weber. It concerns the editing of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke; the previous page is Weber's draft letter to Dumas about borrowing the original Paris prize memoir of 1861.

Summary of the content:
- Dedekind has already sent Weber a parcel containing his own 'Untersuchungen über Riemann's Hypothesen der Geometrie u.s.w.'
- Only afterwards did he remember a later, lengthy exchange of letters with Prof. R. Beez in Plauen im Vogtland. That exchange concerned these topics and especially Weber's editorial 'Note zur Pariser Aufgabe', i.e. Weber's commentary on Riemann's 'Commentatio mathematica, qua respondere tentatur quaestioni ab Ill.ma Academia Parisiensi propositae' on heat conduction and the quadratic differential form.
- Beez had raised various objections to the Note. Dedekind had tried, 'fairly in vain', to dispel them; the exchange cost him much time and brought little reward.
- Dedekind took these letters with him to Harzburg, thinking they could be useful to Weber.

The next page continues the letter: 15 sheets ordered in red ink; a remark on sheet 9 about the theory of linear partial differential equations; a reference to Beez's papers in Schlömilch's Zeitschrift; and a visit by Felix Klein and his wife to Harzburg.

No derivation exists to reconstruct.

results.what: Historical/editorial content: Dedekind's correspondence with R. Beez about Weber's commentary on Riemann's 1861 Paris prize essay on heat conduction, written during preparation of Riemann's Werke (likely the 2nd edition, 1892).
results.modern_name: Editorial history of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke / Commentatio mathematica (Paris prize essay)
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind and Weber (editors of Riemann's Werke); Richard Beez (papers on curvature of higher-dimensional manifolds in Zeitschrift für Mathematik und Physik)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a letter from Dedekind to Weber about editing Riemann's works, not a Riemann manuscript. It contains no mathematics. The Dedekind–Weber collaboration and Beez's critical engagement with the Riemann curvature material are already known.
transcription_corrections: 'Prof. R. Lanz[?] in Plauen i. V.' should almost certainly read 'Prof. R. Beez in Plauen i. V.' (Richard Beez, Gymnasium Plauen im Vogtland). This is consistent with the next page's reference to Beez's papers in Schlömilch's Zeitschrift.
'Harzburg[?]' is correct: 'nach Harzburg', confirmed by the next page.
'Riemann 9' at top left is a later archival pencil note, and '86' is the folio number; neither is part of the letter.
The page is a letter by Dedekind, not by Riemann; the bundle attribution 'R.Waermeleitung' reflects its connection to the Paris heat-conduction prize essay.
